The Richard Dinner Vineyard, one of Sonoma Mountain's older planted sites, gives Hobbs access to vines rooted in rocky volcanic loam — a soil type that naturally limits vigor and concentrates flavor without requiring heavy-handed extraction.\n\nThe Cuvée Agustina represents the top selection from this vineyard. Across vintages from 2014 through 2021, it has consistently earned competition medals (golds in 2014, 2015, 2016; silvers in 2017 and 2021), suggesting a wine that delivers reliably but may vary in intensity with vintage conditions. The 2015 and 2016 vintages, shaped by California's drought years, likely pushed concentration higher, while 2021 — a cooler, drier vintage — probably dialed back toward leaner fruit and more pronounced acidity.",

At around 1,200 feet, Richard Dinner Vineyard gets direct morning sun while the valley floor stays shrouded, giving the vines a longer effective growing day. But the site also benefits from significant diurnal temperature swings — warm afternoons followed by cool nights — which preserves acidity in ways that lower-elevation Sonoma sites struggle to match. The volcanic soils here are rocky and well-drained, forcing roots deep and limiting water availability. In the glass, this translates to a Chardonnay with a mineral backbone — think wet stone and chalk — underneath the stone fruit, rather than the plush, glycerol-heavy texture you'd get from richer clay-dominant valley floor sites.",

Extended lees contact — aging the wine on its spent yeast cells with periodic stirring (bâtonnage) — builds body and a biscuity richness without relying solely on new oak for texture. Seared halibut with brown butter and capers — the brown butter echoes the wine's oak and malo character, while the capers add a brininess that plays off the mineral finish. Mushroom risotto with aged Parmesan — the umami and starch demand a wine with enough body to stand up, and the Chardonnay's acidity resets the palate between bites. parsed.hook: Richard Dinner Vineyard sits at roughly 1,200 feet on Sonoma Mountain's eastern slope — above the fog line that blankets the valley floor each morning. parsed.wine_summary:
Paul Hobbs built his reputation as a winemaker who lets site specificity lead. After stints at Robert Mondavi and Opus One in the 1980s, he launched his own label in 1991 with a focus on vineyard-designated wines that reflect geology rather than formula. The Richard Dinner Vineyard, one of Sonoma Mountain's older planted sites, gives Hobbs access to vines rooted in rocky volcanic loam — a soil type that naturally limits vigor and concentrates flavor without requiring heavy-handed extraction.

The Cuvée Agustina represents the top selection from this vineyard. Across vintages from 2014 through 2021, it has consistently earned competition medals (golds in 2014, 2015, 2016; silvers in 2017 and 2021), suggesting a wine that delivers reliably but may vary in intensity with vintage conditions. The 2015 and 2016 vintages, shaped by California's drought years, likely pushed concentration higher, while 2021 — a cooler, drier vintage — probably dialed back toward leaner fruit and more pronounced acidity.

The volcanic soils here are rocky and well-drained, forcing roots deep and limiting water availability. In the glass, this translates to a Chardonnay with a mineral backbone — think wet stone and chalk — underneath the stone fruit, rather than the plush, glycerol-heavy texture you'd get from richer clay-dominant valley floor sites.
parsed.vinification_summary: Hobbs typically ferments his single-vineyard Chardonnays in French oak barrels — a mix of new and used — with native yeast, which introduces more complexity and textural variation than commercial strains. The wine undergoes full malolactic fermentation (the bacterial conversion of sharp malic acid into softer lactic acid), which rounds out the palate and contributes the creamy, buttery mid-palate the wine is known for. Extended lees contact — aging the wine on its spent yeast cells with periodic stirring (bâtonnage) — builds body and a biscuity richness without relying solely on new oak for texture. The oak program is calibrated to frame rather than dominate: you'll taste vanilla and toast, but they sit behind the fruit and mineral core rather than in front of it.
